$comment: The exact multi-asset symbology and quote vectors (public-chart-library-boundary-plan.md PCL-4
and its acceptance gate: 'Pin exact formatter fixtures for equities, sub-cent crypto, FX and
pips, CME decimal futures, 1/32 and 1/4-of-1/32 futures, and variable tick bands ... Produce
One entry per market shape. `format` is the Quick Charts PriceFormat the datafeed resolves;
`prices` are the display cases the one package formatter must produce, each of which must also
parse back to its own value; `quote` carries the raw quote values a board renders for the same
symbol, so a consumer can prove Last and Chg follow the symbol's price format while Chg% and
Volume keep their own value kinds. Quote values are quote data, never symbology: they are here
as inputs to a display test, not as facts the datafeed's symbology contract owns.
Read by packages/chart/test/priceFormatter.test.ts. The private facade's quote work reuses the
same file rather than inventing a second set of numbers.
punctuation: the punctuation the displays below assume. Absent means the default, which is a
'.' decimal sign and no grouping: the chart writes a price ungrouped.

cases.what: the same equity with a host that asked for grouping and a comma decimal sign
a five-decimal FX pair: pricescale 100000, minmov 1. The pip is the fourth decimal and the fifth is the pipette; both are written, because the price format says five
a yen pair, whose pip is the second decimal: pricescale 1000, minmov 1
a quarter-point CME future: pricescale 100, minmov 25. minmov declares the grid, not the column width
a 1/32 Treasury future: pricescale 32, minmov 1, fractional. The fraction is padded to the width of 31
a 1/4-of-1/32 Treasury future: pricescale 128, minmov 1, minmove2 4, fractional
an ordered tick ladder: 0.0001 below 1, 0.001 below 10, 0.01 at or above 10. The band is a declared symbol fact, so the width changes by band and never by a magnitude guess
